runs.entry: Price **$3.00** (quote of 2026-10-13 through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **141,009,357**, one class (10-Q cover at 2026-07-16, `0001193125-26-314196`; `cover_shares.py` the same; the balance sheet shows 141,010,284 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30, no treasury shares); cap **$423M**; net debt **$9,621M** at 2026-06-30 (principal $9,770M including $298M of finance leases, less cash $149M; operating leases left out). Sovereign **5.60%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (`0001193125-26-059509`), 10-Ks FY2018, FY2021 and FY2023, 10-Q to 2026-06-30, proxy 2026 (`0001193125-26-140269`), the 8-K of 2026-07-22 (cover only); one figure cross-checked (FY2025 operating cash $543M and capex $335M against the filed statement). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the FY2025 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. Competitors: the 10-K names only municipal and not-for-profit hospitals, none an SEC filer, flagged; the analyst took the three hospital companies the proxy names as peers (HCA, Tenet, UHS), from XBRL facts, transcription, flagged. **Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: 69 general acute care hospitals in 14 states, mostly non-urban; Medicare, Medicare Managed Care and Medicaid 51.4% of 2025 revenue at prices the filer says rise less than inflation; the 2025 Reconciliation Law (Medicaid eligibility, provider taxes, state directed payments), expired ACA subsidies and outpatient cuts, of which the filer writes that it "cannot estimate" the effect of changes already enacted; the footprint being sold down to meet the debt (nine hospitals with about $1.6B of 2025 revenue sold in the first half of 2026); owner cash before interest -1.3% to 6.4% of revenue 2021 to 2025, 3.6% average 2022 to 2025; contrary evidence weighed (same-store revenue +4.6% and operating income +7.2% in 2025, an ageing service area, the speakers' rows on health care's political staying power); NATURE because the filer itself declines the deciding forecast. Q2 to Q12 not reached. After the stop: operating margin before impairments and sale gains 7.1% ten-year average against HCA 14.9%, UHS 10.8%, Tenet 10.1% without 2024; equity negative since 2017, assets $21.9B to $12.2B and revenue $18.4B to $12.5B 2016 to 2025, debt down about $5.7B from hospital sales while the deficit deepened about $3.3B; shares up about 25% in ten years; no buyback programme; an impairment-and-sale line every year and Adjusted EBITDA featured; debt principal $9.8B with about $5.3B due 2029 to 2031 and the newest notes at 9.75% to 10.875%, debt 113% of capitalization. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: 2021 aberrational on the filer's own description (Medicare accelerated-payment repayment), central window 2022 to 2025, literal beside; CONVENTIONS of the run confessed: the interest shield at a 25% tax rate, and divestiture proceeds excluded from owner cash with the base restated to the hospitals still owned (revenue $10,885M); growth of 30.9% cut by specific (f) to sales growth of 0.74%; all capex charged (no maintenance split filed); owner cash before interest $391M central; range **-$18.69 to -$15.68 a share all-equity** against $3.00; no case earns the floor (central 3.9% on the $10,044M enterprise, best single year 7.0%); fair **-$39.77 all-equity, none above zero**; equity-only owner cash negative, no positive figure; no alert (box not TOO HARD at a later question nor OUT at Q7). Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the DOJ civil investigative demand of 2024-01-11 on utilization review, inpatient admissions and dialysis; the DOJ criminal investigation of a physician at Northwest Arkansas with Northwest and several current and former officers and employees named as subjects (Northwest sold 2026-06-01); the QHC Litigation Trust suit over the 2016 Quorum spin-off, $1.21B at issue, summary judgment pending; chief executive pay $4.77M for 2025, pay ratio 60:1. Contamination declared by the analyst: a directory listing of `Test Runs/` showing other 2026-10-13 file names (among them ACHC), and the session's git status commit subjects; none opened or used; nothing about CYH seen. Commits 06766245, f9f5d075, 74cf8b13, 66ac2ac9, 41984183. Folded by the 14:46 cycle: the 13:16 cycle dispatched the run and began the fold (position note written, `dispatcher_verify.py` written) when it hit the session limit at 13:31, and the 13:46 and 14:16 cycles were rate limited; the position note it left (not held, read from `PORTFOLIO.md` after the run was committed) was confirmed and committed with this fold. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` passed; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_verify.py` 20 quoted fragments, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q1's routing names fast-moving industries and not a government-set price whose enacted changes the filer cannot estimate; a second analyst could close the name OUT at Q2 or Q7 instead, which changes whether a lower price reopens it; (2) specific (c) is written for a buyer of businesses and would count a seller's divestiture proceeds as owner cash; (3) the brief's rival rule when the 10-K names no SEC filer (the proxy's peers taken); (4) how a fair price is reported when the whole range sits below net debt. Could not get: the maintenance split of capex, the 2021 share-count step's filing, the 8-K earnings exhibits and the rivals' filed 10-Ks.
runs.narr: Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE): the non-urban hospital chain (69 hospitals) with 51.4% of revenue at Medicare and Medicaid prices whose enacted changes under the 2025 law the filer says it cannot estimate, acting on owner cash before interest of about 3.6% of revenue, the footprint sold down to meet $9.8B of debt. After the stop: margin 7.1% over ten years against HCA 14.9%, UHS 10.8%, Tenet 10.1%; equity negative since 2017; shares up about 25% as the business shrank. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range -$18.69 to -$15.68 a share all-equity against $3.00, no case earns the floor, fair none above zero. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: a DOJ civil investigative demand on admissions, a DOJ criminal investigation naming the Northwest Arkansas unit's officers as subjects, the QHC trust suit.
